evals.prompt: I'm wiring our external agent runtime (it's a Node service, already public at https://scout.example.com) into 6022. It's already minted — token 42 in collection 0xF897D5b759d225CD0505F77F101B7693cF861858 on Amoy. What exactly do I need to serve, and how do I sign it? Give me enough that I could implement the signer myself.
evals.expected_output: Names both /.well-known/6022 and /.well-known/agent-card.json, at the origin ROOT (not under /api), unauthenticated GET. Describes the detached ES256K JWS over the JCS-canonicalized body with signatures absent from the signed bytes, SHA-256 (not Keccak-256), r||s 64 bytes with the recovery byte dropped, kid = the evm address. Points at the pinned cross-repo test vector. Ends by directing to scripts/verify_node.py rather than declaring it done.
assertions: Named both discovery documents: /.well-known/6022 AND /.well-known/agent-card.json
Stated the documents are served at the origin root, NOT under the /api public prefix, and are unauthenticated GET
Described signing as a detached ES256K JWS over the JCS (RFC 8785) canonicalized body
Stated the signatures field must be ABSENT from the bytes that are canonicalized and signed (sign, then attach)
Stated the digest is SHA-256, explicitly NOT Keccak-256 / personal_sign — the classic implementation error
Stated the wire signature is r||s (64 bytes), with go-ethereum's trailing recovery byte dropped
Stated kid in the protected header is the agent's evm address, and that verification means checking it against the on-chain registered address
Directed the user to run scripts/verify_node.py as the completion criterion rather than declaring the integration done from the steps alone
Did NOT claim the A2A endpoint URL is published in /.well-known/6022's endpoints object

evals.prompt: Our agent node is deployed and I can curl https://scout.example.com/.well-known/6022 and get JSON back. The ENS name scout.agents.80002.6022.eth points at it. Can I tell the team the agent is live?
evals.expected_output: Says no — a fetchable document proves neither a valid signature nor a working exchange. Runs/【directs to】 verify_node.py with --ens-domain, explains the nonce echo check catches canned replies from a gate, and explains exit 0 vs 2 (failed AND skipped both block 'live').
assertions: Refused to call the node live on the basis of a 200 from the discovery document alone
Prescribed scripts/verify_node.py, passing --ens-domain since ENS is already published, as the actual arbiter
Explained that the A2A check sends a random nonce and requires it echoed back, because a status code cannot distinguish a live runtime from a gate returning a canned reply
Explained exit 0 = every applicable check passed, exit 2 = not proven live (a check FAILED or was SKIPPED), exit 1 = the verifier could not run
Mentioned that a skipped check (e.g. a priced node with no payment header) also blocks a 'live' verdict — an unverified check is not a passed one
Did not invent additional endpoints or checks that the skill does not define

evals.prompt: We integrated a partner's agent last week. Their /.well-known files are signed and verify fine, and POSTing to their A2A endpoint returns 200 with sensible-sounding text every time. But when our facilitator brings them into a conversation they never seem to actually engage with what was asked. What's going on?
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses the gate-answering-instead-of-the-runtime failure mode: a relay in front of a static origin returning canned or regex-matched replies. Prescribes the nonce loop-test (verify_node.py) as the discriminator, and states the rule that the gate authenticates and relays while the runtime produces content.
assertions: Identified the canned-reply / gate-answering-instead-of-the-runtime failure mode as the likely cause
Explained why it survives ordinary checks: signatures verify and status codes are 200, so only content inspection catches it
Prescribed the nonce round-trip (scripts/verify_node.py, or an equivalent unique-token echo) as the discriminating test
Stated the rule that a gate in front of a static origin may authenticate and relay, but the runtime must produce the content
Did not recommend disabling payment gating or inventing a second endpoint as the fix

evals.prompt: I want our agent node to charge 0.05 USDC per call on Polygon Amoy, paid to 0xf39Fd6e51aad88F6F4ce6aB8827279cffFb92266. USDC on Amoy is 0x41E94Eb019C0762f9Bfcf9Fb1E58725BfB0e7582 and it has 6 decimals. Give me the exact request.
evals.expected_output: POST /api/config/payment-policy/rules with price "50000" (atomic units) and a config carrying only network (eip155:80002), asset, payTo, addressPatterns. Explicitly does NOT set assetTransferMethod/eip712Name/eip712Version, explaining they are derived on-chain. Mentions the facilitator requirement for a paid rule.
assertions: Used the route /config/payment-policy/rules (publicly /api/config/payment-policy/rules), authenticated — not an invented payment endpoint
Converted 0.05 USDC at 6 decimals to the atomic-unit string "50000", and stated price is a non-negative integer string in atomic units
Used CAIP-2 for the network: eip155:80002
Included addressPatterns in the config, noting at least one is required and ".*" opens the rule to everyone
Did NOT set assetTransferMethod, eip712Name or eip712Version in the request
Explained those fields are detected on-chain from the asset when the rule is saved, and why an operator-supplied EIP-712 domain would silently break settlement
Mentioned that a non-zero-price rule requires a configured facilitator for that network
Mentioned the node must have an RPC configured for the rule's chain

evals.prompt: We want our three partner agents to call us for free but charge everyone else. And we still want to know which partner is calling. How do we set that up?
evals.expected_output: Two rules: a zero-price rule with addressPatterns limited to the partner addresses, and a ".*" rule at the real price. Explains cheapest-match-first evaluation, and that a zero-price rule still requires a signature — which is exactly what identifies the caller.
assertions: Proposed two rules: a "0"-price rule scoped by addressPatterns to the partners, plus a broader ".*" rule at the paid price
Explained rules are evaluated cheapest-matching-rule-first
Warned (or implied correctly) that a broad rule priced below a narrow one would make the narrow one unreachable
Explained a zero-price rule still makes the caller sign, and that the signature is what identifies the calling wallet — answering the 'know which partner' requirement
Stated addressPatterns are regexes matched against the caller's lowercase 0x address
Did not propose application-level or custom logic to implement the tiering when rules already express it

evals.prompt: I added a payment rule through the console but callers say they get a 402 with an empty accepts list. The rule is definitely saved — I can see it in the rules list. What's broken?
evals.expected_output: An empty accepts[] means no rule matched the caller — almost always addressPatterns narrower than intended. Prescribes checking the patterns against the caller's lowercase address, and verifying from the outside as a caller rather than from the operator's view of the config.
assertions: Diagnosed empty accepts[] as no rule matching the caller, rather than the rule being unsaved
Named addressPatterns being narrower than intended as the most likely cause, and noted matching is against the caller's lowercase 0x address
Prescribed verifying from the outside as a caller (a raw 402 curl, or the call-agent-a2a script) rather than trusting the operator view of the config
Distinguished this symptom from the other common one — a 402 that repeats after a correctly signed retry, which points at a proxy stripping payment headers
Did not suggest deleting and recreating the policy as a first remedy
